title: [Spike] EXPLAIN every search path and prove which ones actually use the vector index
summary: The zero-vector filter wraps a function around the indexed column; if that defeats VECIDX, every published APPROX benchmark number is measuring a table scan.
description:
Highest-priority story in this epic because several others are only worth doing if its answer is bad, and one already-published set of numbers may be wrong if it is.

Run EXPLAIN against a live Db2 12.1.5 with a realistically-sized table (the 500k seed corpus, not a test fixture) for each search shape: EXACT with no filters; APPROX with no filters; APPROX plus scope predicates; APPROX plus `metadata_filter`; APPROX plus `min_confidence`; APPROX with `hybrid=True` and its 4x inflation; and the `_search_via_chunks` path. For each, record whether the access plan shows `VECIDX` / `IXSCAN` or a table scan, the estimated and actual cost, and rows examined.

The specific hypothesis under test: `AND VECTOR_SERIALIZE(embedding) != VECTOR_SERIALIZE(CAST('<zeros>' AS VECTOR(d,FLOAT32)))` — added by ORC-2 for a correct reason (COSINE against a zero vector raises SQL0801N) — is a function-on-indexed-column predicate and may prevent the optimizer choosing `VECIDX`, or force a full FETCH of every candidate. Test by running the identical query with and without that clause and diffing the plans.

Second hypothesis, from published Db2 vector-index testing: on small tables the optimizer legitimately prefers a table scan and needs explicit `OPTGUIDELINES` to use the index at all. If our live-Db2 tests run on small tables, they may be green while never once exercising the index path — which would mean we have no test coverage of the thing we ship.

Timebox: one working session. Output: a findings comment with the plan for every shape, plus stories for whatever it turns up. If the zero-vector filter does defeat the index, VIDX-5 becomes the top priority of this epic and a correction note is owed to `project-management/BENCHMARKS.md`.
